content.value_statement: Energy data projects often lack clear compliance gates and measurable value. This skill structures classification, cash-flow evidence, accounting coordination, and commercialization options.
actual_capabilities: Classifies power, charging, storage, grid, and water data by sensitivity.
Screens projects for personal information, important data, and CII concerns.
Tests cash flows for measurability, sustainability, attribution, and verification.
Designs charging-service revenue-rights and controlled data-use pathways.
Outlines a staged assessment SOP and eleven expected deliverables.
Coordinates accounting, valuation, legal, and cross-border review needs.
limitations: It does not issue binding legal, regulatory, accounting, or valuation opinions.
CII and important-data decisions require current authority guidance and qualified reviewers.
Financial conclusions depend on contracts, bills, logs, baselines, and complete operating data.
RWA structures require jurisdiction-specific review before implementation or promotion.

use_cases.title: Screen a charging portfolio
use_cases.description: Classify charging data, identify privacy concerns, and test whether service-fee cash flows support assetization.

use_cases.title: Evaluate storage value
use_cases.description: Connect storage performance data to maintenance savings, grid services, and evidence-based cash-flow measures.

use_cases.title: Review sensitive grid data
use_cases.description: Identify important-data and CII concerns before proposing internal optimization, controlled services, or cross-border use.

prompt_templates.title: Create a data inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: List our energy datasets by source, fields, update frequency, owner, users, and business purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Classify data sensitivity
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these datasets by sensitivity, personal information, important-data indicators, CII relevance, and required evidence: [datasets].

prompt_templates.title: Test measurable cash flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this scenario for measurable, sustainable, attributable, and verifiable cash flow. State evidence gaps and a proceed, remediate, or stop conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Design an integrated pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a phased pathway for [portfolio], covering compliance gates, revenue rights, privacy controls, valuation inputs, accounting coordination, verification, and approval dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a complex energy data project.

output_examples.input: Assess charging records containing user, payment, vehicle, energy, location, and service-fee data.
output: Classification: charging operations data with personal information.
Primary control: remove direct identifiers and restrict behavior-level disclosures.
Cash-flow basis: service fees supported by contracts, bills, and system logs.
Conclusion: proceed after privacy, rights, and evidence checks.

output_examples.input: Can grid topology and dispatch data be sold or transferred abroad?
output_examples.output: Treat the data as potentially important or CII-related. Pause external transfer, confirm authority rules, and assess controlled internal or statistical use.

output_examples.input: Evaluate storage health data for an accounting and valuation project.
output_examples.output: Link health data to verified maintenance savings or grid-service income. Establish a baseline, document attribution, then engage qualified accounting and valuation reviewers.

best_practices: Complete classification and CII screening before designing commercialization.
Support every cash-flow claim with contracts, bills, logs, and baseline comparisons.
Separate revenue rights from data rights and document each approval.
anti_patterns: Do not treat data volume alone as proof of asset value.
Do not expose identifiable charging behavior or bypass cross-border review.
Do not present preliminary analysis as legal, regulatory, valuation, or accounting approval.

faq.question: What energy data does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers power operations, charging stations, battery storage, grids, and water operations.

faq.question: Does it determine whether data is CII or important data?
faq.answer: It provides an initial screen. Final classification requires current authority rules and qualified review.

faq.question: How does it test assetization feasibility?
faq.answer: It checks whether cash flow is measurable, sustainable, attributable, and verifiable.

faq.question: Can it provide a formal valuation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes evidence and valuation inputs for review by qualified professionals.

faq.question: Can it design a charging station RWA?
faq.answer: It can outline revenue-rights separation, privacy controls, evidence needs, and review steps. Implementation requires jurisdiction-specific legal and financial approval.

faq.question: What information should users provide?
faq.answer: Provide dataset fields, ownership, contracts, bills, logs, processing locations, intended users, transfer plans, and current controls.
